transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Treat this as an electrical hazard.

• Do not touch the dishwasher, plugs, sockets, or any switches near the water.
• Keep everyone, including pets, away from the wet area. Do not walk through the water.
• If you can reach your home’s main electrical consumer unit/fuse box without going near the water, switch off the power to the kitchen or the main supply.
• Do not unplug the dishwasher while the floor is wet or if the plug/socket may be wet.
• If it is safe to do so without approaching electrical outlets, turn off the dishwasher’s water supply valve (usually under the sink). Otherwise, leave it.
• If there is sparking, buzzing, smoke, burning smell, or anyone has had a shock, leave the area and call emergency services/fire service immediately.
• Once power is safely isolated, call an emergency electrician and a plumber/appliance repair technician (or your landlord/building manager if you rent).

The leak could be from a loose or split hose, a failed door seal, blocked drain, or an internal dishwasher fault—but do not investigate until the electrical risk is dealt with.
its still running tho and theres loads of bubbles coming out the door. the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. i dont know where the fuse box is, what do i do

Do not try to stop it using the dishwasher buttons or touch the door, plug, sockets, extension lead, or water.

The water is about to reach an extension lead, so treat this as an immediate electrical emergency:

1. Move people and pets away now. Do not step in the water.
2. Call emergency services now — use your local emergency number (such as 999, 112, or 911) and say:
   “A dishwasher is leaking heavily, still running, and water is spreading toward an extension lead/electrical sockets.”
3. If you can see a water shut-off valve under the sink and can reach it without stepping near or through water and without touching anything electrical, turn it clockwise to stop the water. If not, leave it.
4. Do not mop it up, use towels, unplug anything, move the extension lead, or open the dishwasher door until electricity has been safely isolated.
5. If you know where the main fuse box/consumer unit is and can get to it by a completely dry route, switch off the main power or kitchen circuit. If you do not know where it is, do not search through the wet area—tell emergency services.

If you see sparks, hear crackling/buzzing, smell burning, or smoke starts, get out of the home/area immediately and wait for emergency responders.
